title: Git Basics and GitHub Workflow
description: Learn Git fundamentals — from installing and configuring Git to pushing code on GitHub and handling merge conflicts
objective: Students will install Git, create a repository, make commits, work with branches, push to GitHub, create a pull request, and resolve a merge conflict

steps.title: Install Git and Configure Identity
steps.instructions:
## Install Git

1. Download Git from [git-scm.com/downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads)
2. Run the installer — keep all default options
3. Open a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Git Bash) and verify:

```bash
git --version
```

You should see something like: `git version 2.45.0.windows.1`

## Configure Your Identity

Git needs to know who you are so it can label your commits. Run these commands (use your own name and email):

```bash
git config --global user.name "Rahul Sharma"
git config --global user.email "rahul@techpath.biz"
```

Set the default branch name to `main`:

```bash
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

Set VS Code as the default Git editor:

```bash
git config --global core.editor "code --wait"
```

Verify your configuration:

```bash
git config --list
```

You should see your name, email, and other settings listed.

## Create a GitHub Account

If you don't have one already:
1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com)
2. Click **Sign up** and create a free account
3. Verify your email address

steps.title: Create a Repository and Make First Commits
steps.instructions:
## Create a Project Folder

Open your terminal and run:

```bash
mkdir techpath-portfolio
cd techpath-portfolio
```

## Initialize Git

```bash
git init
```

You should see: `Initialized empty Git repository in .../techpath-portfolio/.git/`

## Create Your First File

Create a file called `README.md` in VS Code (or any editor) with this content:

```markdown
# TechPath Portfolio

A portfolio project built during the Python Full Stack course at TechPath Institute, Bhopal.

## About
This project demonstrates Git and GitHub workflow.
```

Save the file.

## Check Status, Stage, and Commit

```bash
# See the current state — README.md should show as untracked
git status

# Stage the file (add it to the "ready to commit" area)
git add README.md

# Commit with a message
git commit -m "docs: add project README"
```

## Add More Files and Make More Commits

Create `app.py`:

```python
def greet(name):
    return f"Welcome to TechPath Institute, {name}!"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(greet("Rahul"))
    print(greet("Priya"))
```

Stage and commit:

```bash
git add app.py
git commit -m "feat: add greeting function"
```

Create a `.gitignore` file:

```
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
.env
.vscode/
```

Stage and commit:

```bash
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: add .gitignore for Python project"
```

## View Your Commit History

```bash
git log --oneline
```

You should see 3 commits, newest on top. Note the short commit hash (like `a1b2c3d`) next to each message.

steps.title: Create Branches and Merge Changes
steps.instructions:
## Create a Feature Branch

We will add a new feature on a separate branch, keeping `main` untouched.

```bash
# Create and switch to a new branch
git switch -c feature/add-calculator
```

Verify you are on the new branch:

```bash
git branch
# You should see:
#   main
# * feature/add-calculator
```

## Add Code on the Feature Branch

Create `calculator.py`:

```python
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

def subtract(a, b):
    return a - b

def multiply(a, b):
    return a * b

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"5 + 3 = {add(5, 3)}")
    print(f"10 - 4 = {subtract(10, 4)}")
    print(f"6 x 7 = {multiply(6, 7)}")
```

Stage and commit:

```bash
git add calculator.py
git commit -m "feat: add calculator with basic operations"
```

## Switch Back to Main and Verify

```bash
git switch main
```

Check if `calculator.py` exists:

```bash
ls
# calculator.py should NOT be here — it only exists on the feature branch!
```

## Merge the Feature Branch into Main

```bash
# Make sure you are on main
git switch main

# Merge the feature branch
git merge feature/add-calculator
```

Now check:

```bash
ls
# calculator.py should now be here!
```

## Delete the Merged Branch

```bash
git branch -d feature/add-calculator
```

## View the Log with Graph

```bash
git log --oneline --graph --all
```

You should see a clean linear history since this was a fast-forward merge.

steps.title: Push to GitHub and Create a Pull Request
steps.instructions:
## Create a GitHub Repository

1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com) and sign in
2. Click the **+** button (top-right) and select **New repository**
3. Repository name: `techpath-portfolio`
4. Keep it **Public**
5. Do NOT check any initialization options (no README, no .gitignore, no license)
6. Click **Create repository**

## Connect Local to GitHub

GitHub will show you commands. Copy the ones for "push an existing repository":

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/techpath-portfolio.git
git push -u origin main
```

Replace `YOUR-USERNAME` with your actual GitHub username.

Refresh the GitHub page — you should see your files and README!

## Create a Feature Branch for a PR

Let's practice the Pull Request workflow:

```bash
# Create a new feature branch
git switch -c feature/add-utils
```

Create `utils.py`:

```python
def format_currency(amount):
    """Format amount in Indian Rupees."""
    return f"Rs. {amount:,.2f}"

def validate_email(email):
    """Basic email validation."""
    return "@" in email and "." in email

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(format_currency(15999.50))
    print(validate_email("priya@techpath.biz"))
```

Stage, commit, and push the branch:

```bash
git add utils.py
git commit -m "feat: add currency formatter and email validator"
git push -u origin feature/add-utils
```

## Create a Pull Request on GitHub

1. Go to your repository on GitHub
2. You should see a yellow banner: **"feature/add-utils had recent pushes"** — click **Compare & pull request**
3. Fill in the PR:
   - **Title:** `feat: add utility functions`
   - **Description:**
     ```
     ## What does this PR do?
     Adds utility functions for currency formatting and email validation.

     ## Changes
     - Added `format_currency()` for Indian Rupee formatting
     - Added `validate_email()` for basic email checks
     ```
4. Click **Create pull request**
5. Review the changes in the **Files changed** tab
6. Click **Merge pull request** and then **Confirm merge**
7. Click **Delete branch** to clean up

## Pull Changes Locally

```bash
git switch main
git pull
```

Now your local `main` has the merged changes.

steps.title: Handle a Merge Conflict
steps.instructions:
## Set Up the Conflict

We will create two branches that edit the same file on the same line.

```bash
# Make sure you are on main and up to date
git switch main
git pull
```

### Branch 1: Amit's greeting

```bash
git switch -c feature/amit-greeting
```

Edit `app.py` — change the `greet` function's return line to:

```python
def greet(name):
    return f"Namaste {name}! Welcome to TechPath Institute, Bhopal."
```

```bash
git add app.py
git commit -m "feat: update greeting to include Bhopal"
git switch main
```

### Branch 2: Sneha's greeting

```bash
git switch -c feature/sneha-greeting
```

Edit `app.py` — change the same `greet` function's return line to:

```python
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello {name}! Welcome to TechPath Institute, Pune."
```

```bash
git add app.py
git commit -m "feat: update greeting to include Pune"
git switch main
```

## Merge Branch 1 (No Conflict)

```bash
git merge feature/amit-greeting
# This merges cleanly — no conflict
```

## Merge Branch 2 (Conflict!)

```bash
git merge feature/sneha-greeting
# Output: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in app.py
# Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
```

## Resolve the Conflict

Open `app.py` in VS Code. You will see conflict markers:

```python
def greet(name):
<<<<<<< HEAD
    return f"Namaste {name}! Welcome to TechPath Institute, Bhopal."
=======
    return f"Hello {name}! Welcome to TechPath Institute, Pune."
>>>>>>> feature/sneha-greeting
```

Fix it by choosing a combined version. Delete the conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) and write:

```python
def greet(name):
    return f"Namaste {name}! Welcome to TechPath Institute."
```

Save the file.

## Complete the Merge

```bash
# Stage the resolved file
git add app.py

# Commit the merge
git commit -m "fix: resolve greeting merge conflict"
```

## Verify and Push

```bash
# Check the log — you should see the merge commit
git log --oneline --graph

# Push everything to GitHub
git push
```

## Clean Up

```bash
git branch -d feature/amit-greeting
git branch -d feature/sneha-greeting
```

Congratulations! You have resolved your first merge conflict. Take a screenshot of the conflict markers in VS Code and the final resolved code.

expected_output: A GitHub repository with multiple commits following conventional commit format, a merged pull request visible in the PR tab, and a resolved merge conflict in the commit history
